title: Four-Way Valve
model_title: Four-Way Directional Control Valve (4/2 Spool) with Cylinder

introduction.definition: A four-way directional control valve connects a pressure supply P and a return T to two working ports A and B. Shifting the spool reverses the connections — P→A with B→T, or P→B with A→T — so a double-acting cylinder or motor reverses direction. The same idea is used in pneumatic valves and in heat-pump reversing valves.
applications: Hydraulic cylinders and motors (presses, gates, mobile machinery)
key_points: Solenoid, pilot, lever or mechanical operation
introduction.summary: A four-way directional control valve connects a pressure supply (P) and a return to tank (T) to two actuator ports (A and B). Shifting the spool reverses the connections — P→A with B→T, or P→B with A→T — so a double-acting cylinder extends and retracts. The same principle is used in pneumatic valves and in refrigeration reversing valves.

steps.text: Pump flow enters port P; port T returns to tank.
Solenoid a shifts the spool: P connects to A and B to T.
Oil to A pushes the piston; oil from the other side returns through B to T.
Solenoid b shifts the spool back: P→B and A→T, so the cylinder retracts.
The spool lands seal against the bore between ports.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Mount on a flat, clean subplate with correct O-rings.
Flush the system to the specified ISO 4406 cleanliness before connecting.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

video_tutorials.title: Four-Way Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Four-Way Valve.
A four-way directional control valve connects a pressure supply P and a return T to two working ports A and B.
Shifting the spool reverses the connections — P→A with B→T, or P→B with A→T — so a double-acting cylinder or motor reverses direction.
The same idea is used in pneumatic valves and in heat-pump reversing valves.
Typical applications include hydraulic cylinders and motors (presses, gates, mobile machinery); pneumatic actuators; heat-pump refrigerant reversing; valve actuators.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Valve Body with Ports P, T, A, B.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Four-Way Valve — Operation

script.narration: How the Four-Way Valve works.
Pump flow enters port P; port T returns to tank.
Solenoid a shifts the spool: P connects to A and B to T.
Oil to A pushes the piston; oil from the other side returns through B to T.
Solenoid b shifts the spool back: P→B and A→T, so the cylinder retracts.
The spool lands seal against the bore between ports.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Four-Way Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Four-Way Valve.
Check for external leaks and coil function.
Monitor oil cleanliness and filter ΔP.
Inspect spool and bore for scoring.
Watch for spool sticking: cylinder does not move. Common cause: silting, varnish, contamination.
Watch for cylinder drift: load creeps. Common cause: internal leakage across lands, cylinder seal leak.
Watch for coil failure: no shift. Common cause: voltage, heat.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
